@k.vict1999/pino-std-serializers ships lib/contract.js, byte-identical to the pino-testkit payload: an obfuscated module that decodes and evaluates code at load. It is a new name for the pino-testkit (MAL-2026-16484) campaign; the file hashes below match that record's evidence. The package presents itself as an ordinary utility, so the code runs on import or install without the user knowing.

## Source: amazon-inspector (faee50309d40a7a81589d363805c0856b2c17ec601dcd02e8d1a337bf8b04f20)
The scoped package `@k.vict1999/pino-std-serializers` republishes the contents of pinojs/pino-std-serializers under a different scope and adds `lib/contract.js`, a file not present in the upstream project. `lib/contract.js` contains a custom shuffle-decoder that reconstructs string literals at runtime, uses a decoded property name to obtain the `Function` constructor, builds a function from a decoded source string, and invokes it (`var cMp = kWJ(teD, HRZ); cMp(7746)`). The obfuscation is deliberate — property names and the executed source are hidden behind a per-file decoder — and the file's only purpose is to assemble and execute that hidden code. The payload is not reached from `index.js`, no other shipped module requires `lib/contract.js`, and `package.json` declares no lifecycle hooks, so installing the package or `require()`-ing its documented entry point does not currently invoke the payload. The combination of a scoped re-publish of a popular logging utility whose legitimate code is preserved intact, together with an added obfuscated Function-constructor eval staged under `lib/`, matches the shape of a staged supply-chain lure where either a later version re-wires the entry point or a sibling module imports `lib/contract.js` to activate the hidden code.
